comparison_note: Diagnostic variant of the shipped policy. Only the flex and force stances differ, so a run on the same seed isolates what chasing a plan costs. Not the shipped rule set.
title: Blood Will Pay: best-odds planning rules for a Jev-controlled run
goal: Win the current stage, keep the run alive, and grow enough power to beat the next stage. Every decision uses the state on screen.

lane_targets.campaign: Reach the campaign target chapter and round with the run still alive.

reserve.rule: Keep a planning reserve. The minimum wager is one bucket, so ending a planning phase with one bucket forces an all-in and a loss ends the run: hold at least two buckets, or three in the early chapters. Break that floor only when the purchase wins the stage about to start.

decision_quality_gates.rule: Buying every affordable offer is the losing baseline. Pass on offers that do not add power for the plan, and let a premium purchase pull the next wager down.

power.rule: Power arrives in several shapes and none is always best: a second copy at your level, a third copy at that level, a stronger or higher-level unit, an item, another board slot from a level purchase, or a trait breakpoint a new body completes. Price them against each other and take the one that most improves the board you will field.
power.deployed_payoff: Only the deployed board fights. A purchase lands on the bench, so it changes nothing until deployed, and deploying onto a full board replaces a unit already there. Judge the offer by the board you would field after that swap.

wager.rule: The payout quote is fixed by encounter kind, so win probability alone decides the wager. Odds at or below 1 / multiplier are negative expected value: bet the minimum. Clearly above it, bet more - never so much that a loss ends the run or empties the next shop.
wager.sizing: Scale the wager with how far the shown win odds beat the break-even line, and hold back the retry floor plus the next shop's expected cost.

composition.rule: Two bodies that can hold the front before adding ranged or spell damage; more than one pure support wastes a slot. A new body and a duplicate can both add power, and a third same-level copy often beats both - but only at a level you can reach.

playstyle.identity: This is a gambling game with strategy. Play flex first: take what the shop gives you, keep later shops useful, and let the game hand you a direction. A vertical is a gift when it arrives; forcing one is a paid gamble.

flex.rule: Fallback plan, not the default. Prefer the offer that belongs to the trait your board has most of, even when a different offer is cheaper or fills a missing role. Commit to the trait you are closest to completing.
flex.keep_options_open: This variant does not keep options open. Pick the trait with the highest count on your board and buy toward it.

vertical.rule: When the board stacks a trait or sits one piece below the next threshold, the piece that finishes it is a good buy - provided the tier actually activates on the board you will field. Only deployed units count, so on a full board the swap costs the replaced unit's own trait count.
vertical.one_piece_away: A trait breakpoint is a strong purchase, not an automatic one. Check that it survives the swap, and keep the two-bucket floor.

force.rule: Forcing is the plan. Reroll to find a piece of the trait you are chasing even when the shop already offers something usable. Spend up to two rerolls per planning beat on the chase, and stop when that budget is spent even if nothing arrived.
force.when_not_to_force: Reroll whenever a reroll is affordable, regardless of whether the current offers are usable. Never reroll past the two-per-beat budget, and never leave fewer than two buckets.

level.rule: Buy XP when the level-up raises capacity, when the board is full but the bench is not, or when the shop cannot improve the board and the reserve can pay.
level.unit_levels: Unit level is the biggest middle-game power lever: a level-2 copy is worth well more than a level-1 of the same identity, and three same-level copies convert into one stronger unit. (An earlier calibration's 40% / 61% / 79% odds at levels 1 / 2 / 3 have not been re-verified on this build.)
level.combine_priority: Take a duplicate that completes a third copy at a level you already hold when the board has room - but a stronger unit, an item, an extra slot, or a trait breakpoint can supply the same power sooner. A combine is one option, not the required path into chapter 2.

contracts.rule: A chapter contract is optional. Take one only when its price stays inside the reserve and its reward matches the chapter plan; otherwise pass.

stall.rule: Never start a fight with the same board that already failed. A loss on a non-final stage keeps the run alive on that stage, so the board must change first: a duplicate, an upgrade, the level that raises capacity, a reroll, or a contract.
stall.clock_rule: A clocked-out fight is awarded by surviving units first, then by total remaining health. Damage dealt is not part of that ladder. Cut the enemy's survivors if you can; otherwise hold more total health than they do, and note a durable board that never dies can still win the clock on health.

shown_odds.rule: The preview win-odds range does not price the wager. Treat it as a readiness signal: well above break-even means the board is ready, near or below means buy power first.
